thread:
maria (support): Tess from ArcadiaHealth reports that their inbound webhooks to our hosted callback endpoint started failing around 23:50 UTC with 403s. They said nothing changed on their side.
alex (eng-oncall): Noted. Can you paste a sample webhook ID and the customer IPs seeing the 403? Any client TLS errors in their logs?
maria (support): Sample webhook id: wh_01GZZZ9. Customer logs show our request source IPs are 34.88.112.9 and 34.88.112.11 (x-forwarded-for from our side). They pasted this error: "TLS handshake failed: certificate verify failed" occasionally, but mostly 403 Forbidden.
tess (ArcadiaHealth): FWIW we did not change our firewall rules. We allow a handful of Redwood IPs. We see a sudden block against 34.88.112.0/24 starting ~23:45 UTC.
alex (eng-oncall): Okay. Deploy bot ran a scale/balance job at 2026-03-16 23:40 UTC that rotated the shared SNAT pool for some VPC tenants. I'll check the NAT mapping logs.
alex (eng-oncall): jo, can you pull the SNAT allocation history for the private VPC for customer ArcadiaHealth (tenant id: t-arc-92)?
jo (networking): Pulling. Quick summary: we had an automatic SNAT rebalancing that moved several sessions from the previous egress pool (34.88.112.0/28) into the new ephemeral pool (54.213.7.0/28) at 23:42 UTC. Logs: ```
2026-03-16T23:42:03Z rotate_snat_pool tenant=t-arc-92 old_pool=34.88.112.0/28 new_pool=54.213.7.0/28 reason=auto_rebalance
2026-03-16T23:42:04Z apply_iptables_snat tenant=t-arc-92 success=true
```
maria (support): Tess, do you have the allowlist the security team uses? Can you confirm whether 54.213.7.0/28 is present?
tess (ArcadiaHealth): We only had the older block 34.88.112.0/28 in our firewall rules. We just added 54.213.7.0/28 and still seeing intermittent 403s for a minute, then cleared.
alex (eng-oncall): That matches — customer allowlist not updated causing short-term rejects while rotation happened. Two action items: 1) We should have notified customers who use static allowlists about the SNAT rotation window. 2) Offer a dedicated egress IP (sticky SNAT) for tenants with strict firewalls.
maria (support): I already opened a ticket and offered ArcadiaHealth a dedicated egress assignment. They accepted an interim workaround: add both pools to their firewall and retry. They confirmed green at 00:03 UTC.
jo (networking): Internal follow-ups: tweak rotation process to emit an email + console banner for tenants with private VPCs and customers flagged as "static-egress-allowlist". Also add a short TTL blacklist to avoid rotating immediately after recent customer changes.
alex (eng-oncall): Also adding an operational runbook step: when we rotate shared SNAT, post a message in #support and include the new IPs and exact window. That would have prevented this.
deploy-bot: scale/rotate job completed: rotate_snat_pool tenant=t-arc-92 status=done duration=12s
maria (support): Marking resolved with customer confirmation. Will follow up for dedicated egress onboarding. Closing thread in support after the dedicated egress PR is scheduled.
